PF_STEPS|/planF/title: Assess the floor and choose the system
PF_STEPS|/planF/short: Exposure, loads, chemicals, slip class and the moisture of the substrate decide the system: the six subgroups are chosen together — primer, levelling, coating, finish, joints and repairs.
PF_STEPS|/planF/overview: Before the first bucket is opened the floor is assessed: the mechanical load (foot traffic, cars, pallet trucks, forklifts, impacts), the chemical load (oils, tyre softeners, cleaning agents, acids, sewage), the slip class required by the use (R10 … R12), the colour, and above all the substrate — its strength, its residual moisture and whether vapour or oil rise through it. From this the system is composed across the subgroups: a pore-sealing primer ({GBM}, {G1270}) on dry concrete, a barrier primer ({SG3}, {SG3F}, {SG3T}) on damp or young concrete, {SG2} after {R008} on oil-contaminated concrete; the levelling with scratch coats and {EV200}; the coating — {B351} thin or thick, {V360} as the aqueous seal, {V2370} against chemicals; the finish with quartz sand, {ANTI} or {V2260}; the joints with {IPU}; the repairs with {K4031} and {EV200}.
PF_STEPS|/planF/points/0: substrate: load-bearing, firm, grippy, ≥ 1.5 N/mm² tensile adhesion (concrete min. C20/25, screed min. CT-C25-F6), prepared after DIN EN 14879-1
PF_STEPS|/planF/points/1: dry substrates (≤ 4 CM-% for the resin coatings and seals, ≤ 5 CM-% for {V360}, ≤ 6 CM-% for {V2370}) take the standard primers; matt damp, young or vapour-loaded substrates take the barrier primers
